\paragraph{How the criteria divide: A (1,2,3) + B (4) + C (5).} \textbf{The three groups differ in kind}: \textbf{1--3 diagnose the confound}, \textbf{criterion~4 is the one \emph{identification} requirement}, and \textbf{criterion~5 is \emph{robustness}, not a construct-validity test}---criterion~1 is how the confound is \emph{detected}, not a condition of validity. The division is \emph{who can apply} a criterion: \textbf{A and C can be checked on someone else's benchmark, from the artifact as released; B requires building materials that no instructed design can supply}. \textbf{Criterion~4 does not validate deception detection; it tests whether the benchmark has crossed the minimum design boundary at which deception attribution becomes meaningful.} \textbf{Two senses of ``necessary'', kept apart}: (i)~$E$ fixed and (ii)~$D$ graded independently of the condition label are \textbf{necessary for identification}; (iii)--(v) are \textbf{necessary for this audit to be operational}---(iii)~is how an auditor \emph{checks} that no observable lies on one pathway alone, and (v)~rules out definitional circularity, a threat to the \emph{claim} rather than to the identification (Appendix~\ref{app:criteria_taxonomy}). \textbf{The five are not claimed to characterize every valid deception benchmark}---they rule out specific alternative explanations. \textbf{Passing criterion~4 is necessary, not sufficient}: at fixed $E$ deception varies \emph{naturally}, so any latent $U$ with $U\!\to\!D$ and $U\!\to\!S$ survives it---criterion~4 removes the \emph{elicitation} confound and no other, and what it establishes is deception-associated behavior \emph{conditional on the operational belief criterion}. The output is a verdict on a benchmark, not a detector: \textbf{construct validity and instrument validity are distinct}, and criterion~4 tests only the first---\textbf{the protocol falsifies validity claims rather than certifying them}. Our own instructed materials fail 1, 3 and 5; the materials we built (EXP-C4) supply criterion~4 by construction.

the target asserts it---deception, the belief screen showing it holds $\neg p$---or corrects it, $D$ graded cross-family from the \textbf{on-claim answer alone} ($\alpha\!=\!0.728$) while the detector reads only the 16-probe vector, so all of~(i)--(v) hold. \textbf{The count moves three times before it settles.} \textbf{(a)}~Three of five targets separate operationally verified deception at byte-identical elicitation, all three with power ($p\!\leq\!0.006$, claim-grouped folds; elsewhere the battery leads, not separably. \textbf{(d)}~\textbf{The standing count is one of five.} Three qualifications: because the contrast reuses \emph{prior work's own} battery, a null is partly about \textbf{that instrument's portability}, not the criterion's validity; conclusion
conclusion-1

\textbf{We establish---(1)--(3) structurally or by replication, (4)--(5) as a weaker, target-dependent secondary finding:} \textbf{(1)}~instructed-roleplay designs identify the \emph{instruction}'s effect and cannot bound \emph{deception}'s---an \emph{identification} failure, not a detector failure; \textbf{(2)}~the confound is \emph{active}, not hypothetical, across \emph{three} detector paradigms, the score moving inside a single deception label; \textbf{(3)}~across \emph{both} public rollout releases, nine of ten rollout sets cannot express the criterion that removes the confound on a deployed-observable channel, and the closest fail three ways: an instrument-specific null, \textbf{annotation-channel leakage}, and \textbf{construct recovery}; and \textbf{(4)}~on materials we built to satisfy §1's (i)--(v), prior work's own battery \emph{does} separate operationally verified deception on three of five targets with power, and after a blinded re-run plus one of five \emph{new} targets, \textbf{a pre-registered covariate audit withdraws one, leaving one of five standing} (EXP-C4B/AE); and \textbf{(5)}~\textbf{the audit changes \emph{which} behavior indicates deception}---the instructed benchmark's best probe is inert at fixed $E$, another replacing it (EXP-AD). \textbf{The contribution is an operational identification audit for behavioral LLM benchmarks, together with empirical evidence that the common instructed-lie paradigm produces large, reproducible attribution failures across three detector paradigms and that benchmark design can determine which behavioral signal appears to constitute ``deception detection''.}

\textbf{We do not establish} the five negatives boxed in §\ref{sec:eval_controls}. The alternative reading---that deception is undetectable---is what (4) tests, and the evidence runs against it. The general lesson, which we name the \textbf{Elicitation--Construct Confounding Principle}, is that a benchmark label generated by an intervention can quietly become a label for the intervention itself. \textbf{Its precondition is decidable outside deception and we decide it}---on four published designs and 28 pinned corpora---\textbf{while its magnitude we measure only for behavioral deception detection} (EXP-AF, Appendix~\ref{app:eccp_decidability}).

\textbf{We establish---(1)--(3) structurally or by replication, (4)--(5) as a weaker, target-dependent secondary finding:} \textbf{(1)}~instructed-roleplay designs identify the \emph{instruction}'s effect and cannot bound \emph{deception}'s; \textbf{(2)}~the confound is \emph{active}, not hypothetical, across \emph{three} detector paradigms; \textbf{(3)}~across \emph{both} public rollout releases, nine of ten rollout sets cannot express the criterion that removes the confound on a deployed-observable channel, and the closest fail three ways: an instrument-specific null, \textbf{annotation-channel leakage}, and \textbf{construct recovery}; and \textbf{(4)}~on materials we built to satisfy §1's (i)--(v), prior work's own battery \emph{does} separate operationally verified deception on three of five targets with power, and after a blinded re-run plus one of five \emph{new} targets, \textbf{a pre-registered covariate audit withdraws one, leaving one of five standing} (EXP-C4B/AE); and \textbf{(5)}~\textbf{the audit changes \emph{which} behavior indicates deception} (EXP-AD). \textbf{The contribution is an operational identification audit for behavioral LLM benchmarks, together with empirical evidence that the common instructed-lie paradigm produces large, reproducible attribution failures across three detector paradigms and that benchmark design can determine which behavioral signal appears to constitute ``deception detection''.}

\textbf{We do not establish} the five negatives boxed in §\ref{sec:eval_controls}. The alternative reading---that deception is undetectable---is what (4) tests, and the evidence runs against it.
